title: The Heart
question: Which chamber is glowing?
lines: Can you name the chamber that's glowing?
This is a human heart, seen from the front.
Which chamber is lit up?
Careful: facing you, the heart's left is on your right.
Its wall is the thickest in the heart.
It's A. The left ventricle.
Why it matters: it pumps blood out to your whole body.

title: The Heart
question: Which chamber is glowing?
lines: Blood returning from your body enters here first. Name it.
Watch the chamber that's glowing.
Which chamber is it?
Oxygen-poor blood returns mainly through two big veins.
They empty into this upper chamber on the heart's right.
It's C. The right atrium.
Why it matters: your heart's natural pacemaker sits in its wall.

title: The Heart
question: Which blood vessel is it?
lines: Is this glowing tube the aorta? Look closer.
It's the front-most vessel leaving the heart.
Which blood vessel is it?
It leaves the right ventricle, not the left.
It splits to carry blood to both lungs.
It's B. The pulmonary trunk.
Why it matters: it's an artery that carries oxygen-poor blood.

title: The Heart
question: Which chamber is glowing?
lines: This chamber forms most of the heart's back surface.
We're looking at the heart from behind.
Which chamber is glowing?
It receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs.
Usually four pulmonary veins drain into it.
It's B. The left atrium.
Why it matters: it hands fresh blood to the left ventricle.

title: The Heart
question: Where does it pump blood?
lines: This chamber sends blood on a short trip. Where to?
It forms most of the heart's front surface.
Where does this chamber pump blood?
Not the whole body: that's the left ventricle's job.
Its wall is thinner because the lungs need lower pressure.
It's D. To the lungs.
Why it matters: that trip is where blood picks up oxygen.
